newsitem.title: FRANCE: EP wants clear rules on European party funding.
newsitem.headline: EP wants clear rules on European party funding.

text.p: European political parties should have a clear legal status and clear rules on funding, the European Parliament said on Tuesday, in a move designed to improve the credibility of Europe's political institutions.

Euro-MPs approved a report by Greek Socialist Dimitris Tsatsos which urges the European Union to adopt legally-binding acts which detail the status of European parties and the financial support they can receive.

In future, contributions to European political parties from EU funds should be clearly indicated in the EU budget, the Euro-MPs insisted, adding that the EU should give money only to parties that disclosed all their revenue.

In order to benefit from the statutory rights of a European political party -- such as the right to establish, take action and nominate candidates for election -- political organisations should be represented in the European Parliament and at least a third of EU member states, the Euro-MPs said.
These parties must also have views on European policies and be democratically organised to qualify, the Parliament added.
In addition, Tsatsos's report demands that they open up their membership to individuals, not just national political parties, as is the case at present.
European political parties were recognised for the first time by the Maastricht Treaty, signed in 1992.
